export const meta = {
  name: 'v5-typography-and-gap-verifiers',
  description: 'Author explicit per-brand typography for all 100 tasks and fill the 68 remaining K-question verifier gaps across 38 tasks',
  phases: [{ title: 'Author', detail: '20 agents x 5 tasks' }],
}

const SCR = '/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-dhiren-Downloads-Deccan/aa9e6dfc-7579-493e-a3a8-45be309ed406/scratchpad/kfix'
const pad = n => String(n).padStart(2, '0')
const IDS = []
for (let i = 1; i <= 30; i++) IDS.push('PHOTO-' + pad(i))
for (let i = 1; i <= 15; i++) IDS.push('VECTOR-' + pad(i))
for (let i = 1; i <= 35; i++) IDS.push('LAYOUT-' + pad(i))
for (let i = 1; i <= 20; i++) IDS.push('MOTION-' + pad(i))
const BATCHES = []
for (let i = 0; i < IDS.length; i += 5) BATCHES.push(IDS.slice(i, i + 5))

const SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    files_written: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    tasks_done: { type: 'number' },
    verifiers_authored: { type: 'number' },
    notes: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['files_written', 'tasks_done'],
}

function prompt(ids) {
  return `You are doing two precise jobs on a professional creative-AI benchmark. Change NOTHING else: do not touch briefs, deliverables, assets or existing verifiers.

JOB 1 - EXPLICIT TYPOGRAPHY (every task).
Today each brand's typography is vague prose like "a clean grotesque for names, a quiet serif for detail". A designer cannot execute that and a reviewer cannot check it. Rewrite it so it names the ACTUAL type system, the way a real brand guideline does.

Your typography value must state, in plain professional prose (no bullet lists, no dashes):
- The exact display/heading typeface by name, with its family and weight, e.g. "Playfair Display (serif), 700 weight".
- The exact body/text typeface by name, family and weight.
- Any third face if the brand genuinely needs one (numerals, captions, labels).
- Concrete SIZES for the main uses, in the unit that fits the medium: pt for print deliverables, px for screen deliverables. Give real numbers, e.g. "headline 42 pt, subhead 18 pt, body 10.5 pt with 14 pt leading" or "headline 64 px, body 18 px".
- A short statement of what to use where, and one thing NOT to do (e.g. "never set the wordmark in the body face", "no italics on the price").
- Where a distinctive treatment defines the brand, say so explicitly, the way one would say a certain cola brand is a red script with a high-waisted flourish.

Choose faces that genuinely suit this brand, vertical, price band and audience, and that a designer could actually license (real, well known families: e.g. Playfair Display, Söhne, GT Sectra, Inter, Neue Haas Grotesk, Freight Text, Canela, Untitled Sans, Tiempos, Suisse Int'l, National,格 avoid). Do NOT invent fictional font names. Do not reuse the same pairing across all your tasks; match each brand.
Keep it to 45 to 90 words. No em dashes or en dashes anywhere.

JOB 2 - FILL THE REMAINING RUBRIC GAPS (only for tasks that list them).
Each input file has "questions_needing_a_human_verifier". For EACH listed question id, author one or two new atomic human verifiers so the question is genuinely answered for that task. These questions are NOT covered by the automatic layer, so a real observable human check is required.

What each question means:
- K1_Q3 Constraint compliance: a must or must-not the brief imposes, e.g. a claim that may not appear, a supplied element that must be preserved, a production rule.
- K1_Q5 Critical failure: a single requirement whose breach alone makes the commission unusable (wrong allergen, wrong price, wrong recipient name, unplayable file).
- K2_Q1 Asset selection: the correct supplied asset was used for this output.
- K2_Q2 Asset preservation: a supplied locked asset appears unaltered, not redrawn or regenerated.
- K2_Q3 Brand-system compliance: the brand's fonts, palette colours or logo usage are correctly applied. Use the typography you just authored and the brand palette hexes, and name them exactly.
- K2_Q4 Identity fidelity: the product, person or mark is still recognizably the same as in the supplied source.
- K5_Q1 Primary-message recovery: framed objectively, e.g. the named headline is the largest text on the file, or the named subject occupies more area than all text.
- K5_Q2 Information hierarchy: a named element is larger than or sits above another named element.

VERIFIER RULES (identical to the rest of the corpus, the auditors approved this format):
- ONE observable fact about ONE named deliverable. Never club two conditions. Never "each"/"every"/"all outputs" across files.
- Name the deliverable exactly once as \u201cDeliverable name\u201d (filename.ext), taken from the outputs list.
- Quote exact expected values in \u201ccurly quotes\u201d: the headline, the claim, the colour name and hex, the typeface name.
- Plain words, present tense, at most 28 words, answerable Yes or No by looking at that one file.
- NO em dashes or en dashes anywhere. Use commas, colons or parentheses.
- Do not duplicate anything the automatic layer measures (file exists, decodes, pixel or mm dimensions, page count, duration, codec, frame rate, transparency, exact record text).

For each task id in ${JSON.stringify(ids)}: Read ${SCR}/in/<TASK_ID>.json, then Write ${SCR}/out/<TASK_ID>.json containing exactly:
{"task_id":"...",
 "typography":"the rewritten explicit typography string",
 "new_verifiers":[{"output_id":"...","k_id":"...","text":"...","evidence":"..."}]}
If a task lists no questions needing verifiers, still write the file with "new_verifiers": [].

Return only the structured summary.`
}

phase('Author')
const results = await parallel(BATCHES.map((ids) => () =>
  agent(prompt(ids), { label: `author:${ids[0]}..${ids[ids.length-1]}`, phase: 'Author', agentType: 'general-purpose', schema: SCHEMA })
))
const ok = results.filter(Boolean)
return { batches: results.length, null_batches: results.length - ok.length,
  tasks: ok.reduce((s, r) => s + (r.tasks_done || 0), 0),
  verifiers: ok.reduce((s, r) => s + (r.verifiers_authored || 0), 0) }
summary: Author explicit per-brand typography for all 100 tasks and fill the 68 remaining K-question verifier gaps across 38 tasks
